name: Mississippi
tagline: From Delta cotton and Natchez bluffs to Gulf beaches and the Stennis rocket country.
intro: Mississippi's byways follow the river through the Delta and the loess bluffs, wind through the national forests of the hill country, and run along the Gulf shore from Bay St. Louis to Gulfport. This chapter follows the Mississippi Scenic Byways Program of the Mississippi Department of Transportation, which lists the Great River Road and the Natchez Trace Parkway beside its own routes. A road becomes a state byway by act of the Legislature once an advisory committee approves its corridor plan, and the river road is counted twice, as one national byway and as two state byways, the Mississippi Delta Great River Road and the Lower Mississippi Historic Byway.

members.name: Beach Boulevard Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Old Highway 1 runs thirteen miles along the Hancock County shore from Cedar Point through Bay St. Louis and Waveland to the fishing village of Bayou Cadet, past the old Customs House and Buccaneer State Park.

members.name: Brice's Crossroads Battlefield-Chief Tishomingo Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From the battlefield museum in Baldwyn, MS 370 and county roads cross the ground where Forrest met Sturgis in June 1864, with granite markers by the road and a footbridge over Tishomingo Creek, then run on to Guntown.

members.name: Byways to Space Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Six oak-shaded roads cross the 125,000-acre buffer zone around NASA's Stennis rocket test center, each named for a place such as Logtown or Napoleon that was closed when the zone was drawn.
members.note: Shown on the map as NASA Scenic Byway to Space.

members.name: Delta Bluffs Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Three short branches in DeSoto County run from Hernando's historic districts out through rolling farmland to Arkabutla Lake and along Delta Bluff Road, where the hills fall away to the flat delta at Walls.
members.note: No route line: the national dataset does not include this road and the state publishes no map line for it.

members.name: Grand Gulf-Raymond Scenic Byway
members.blurb: An old Civil War road leaves the Grand Gulf military park by the river and climbs through fern-hung loess cuts under moss-draped oaks and cypress, then keeps to high ground for forty miles east to Raymond.

members.name: Great River Road
members.blurb: US 61 and MS 1 follow the river down the western edge of the state, from Delta fields of cotton and soybeans and the blues museum in Clarksdale down to the Vicksburg battlefield and the antebellum houses of Natchez.

members.name: Gulf Coast Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US 90 runs about eighteen miles along the beachfront through Pass Christian, Long Beach and Gulfport, past old downtowns and National Register districts that lost many old buildings to Hurricane Katrina in 2005.
members.note: No route line: the national dataset does not include this road and the state publishes no map line for it.

members.name: Gateway to History
members.blurb: Two-lane roads cross rural Madison County from the Mannsdale-Livingston preservation district to the petrified forest near Flora and the courthouse town of Canton, then run down MS 43 to the Natchez Trace.
members.note: No route line: the national dataset does not include this road and the state publishes no map line for it.

members.name: Highway 605 Scenic Byway
members.blurb: An expressway runs fifteen miles north from US 90 at the Gulfport shore across I-10 to MS 67, past Mississippi Power's Plant Jack Watson; until 2004 its two halves carried the numbers 975 and 981.
members.note: No route line: the national dataset does not include this road and the state publishes no map line for it.

members.name: Highway 67 Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A four-lane highway opened in 2007 runs about twenty-one miles from US 49 at Saucier through the De Soto National Forest to D'Iberville, across country where the potter George Ohr once dug his clay.
members.note: No route line: the national dataset does not include this road and the state publishes no map line for it.

members.name: Lower Mississippi Historic Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US 61 runs more than a hundred miles from Vicksburg south through Port Gibson and Natchez to Woodville, with a side road out past Alcorn State to the ruins of Windsor.

members.name: Mississippi Delta Great River Road Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From the Helena bridge, MS 1 and US 61 run some 175 miles down through Coahoma, Bolivar and Washington counties to the Warren line, with the river levee standing behind the cotton fields much of the way.

members.name: Natchez Trace Parkway
members.blurb: The parkway follows the line of the old Natchez Trace, a route of American Indians and Kaintucks, for about 312 of its 444 miles across Mississippi, from Natchez northeast past Tupelo.

members.name: Noxubee Hills Route
members.blurb: Forty-three miles of rolling woods, fourteen of them unpaved, run from Choctaw Lake through the Tombigbee National Forest past Bluff Lake on the Noxubee refuge to US 45, in old mill country once worked by artesian wells.
members.note: No route line: the national dataset does not include this road and the state publishes no map line for it.

members.name: William Faulkner Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Highway 30 runs 15.7 miles through the Holly Springs National Forest between New Albany and Oxford, past Puskus Lake and the Little Tallahatchie to the mule farm Faulkner kept near the county line.
members.note: No route line: the national dataset does not include this road and the state publishes no map line for it.
